info.title: Relavoi API
info.summary: Phone number masking for Nigerian platforms.
info.description:
Relavoi connects two people by phone without either seeing the other's
number. You create a session for a pair of Nigerian mobile numbers, we
allocate a proxy number, and each party dials that proxy instead.

## Authentication

Every endpoint except `/health` and `/auth/*` takes a bearer JWT.

There are two kinds, and they are not interchangeable:

- An **SDK token**, from `POST /auth/token` with your API key and secret.
  This is what a mobile app or your backend uses to create sessions.
- A **dashboard token**, from `POST /auth/dashboard/login`. Some endpoints
  are dashboard-only, and some are restricted further by the user's role.

Tokens last 15 minutes. Mint a new one rather than trying to refresh.

## Conventions

- Timestamps are ISO 8601 with a `Z` offset.
- Phone numbers are Nigerian mobile numbers. `+2348012345678`,
  `08012345678` and `8012345678` are all accepted and normalised to E.164.
  Anything else is refused with `422 number-not-supported`.
- Money is an object: integer `kobo`, a formatted `display`, and `naira`.
- Lists are cursor-paginated. Pass `pagination.after` back as `after`.
- Errors are RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`.

bearerAuth.description:
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. An SDK token from `POST /auth/token`
or a dashboard token from `POST /auth/dashboard/login`.

detail.description:
Safe to show a user. It never contains a value the caller sent: a
phone number in a rejected field is described, not echoed.

kobo.description: Integer kobo, as a string because it can exceed 2^53.

after.description: Cursor for the next page, or null at the end.

DirectionMode.description:
Which way a call may travel. `A_TO_B_ONLY` lets the agent reach the
customer and refuses the reverse.

proxyNumber.description: The number both parties dial. E.164.

agentPhoneMasked.description:
Masked for display. The real number is never returned by this API,
to anyone, including you.

recordingEnabled.description: Always false. Recording is not available.

recordingUrl.description: Always null. Recording is not available.

supportPhone.description:
Dialled by the carrier for `REDIRECT_SUPPORT`. A Nigerian mobile or
landline, since a support line often is not a mobile.

pushConfig.description: Stored and writable. Nothing reads it yet.

subject.description: The number, masked. Never returned whole.

VerificationResult.description:
Whether a call this device is on really came through one of your
sessions. The SDKs turn this into the green or red banner.

context.description: A line to show the user, when verified.

WebhookConfig.description:
One destination per tenant, not a list of subscriptions. The secret is
never returned; `hasSecret` says whether one is set.

DeliveryLog.description: One attempt to deliver one event to your endpoint.

outcome.description:
Why it ended. `delivered`, `refused`, `timeout` or `blocked`;
`blocked` means the destination failed the SSRF guard.

statusCode.description:
What your endpoint answered. Null means we never got a response,
which is a different fact from a 502.

status.description: The server's judgement on whether you can place calls.

metrics.description:
Counters for the window. `sms_sent`, `sms_received` and
`recording_minute` are always zero: neither feature is available.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but not allowed to do this.

NotFound.description: No such object, or not yours.

Validation.description: The request body or query failed validation.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. `retry-after` says when to come back.

get.description: No auth. Reports whether Postgres and Redis are reachable, and the commit the running image was built from.

200.description: Healthy, or healthy enough to answer.

get.description:
`CLOSED` is normal. `OPEN` means the carrier is failing and new session
creation is refused; there is one provider, so nothing is rerouted.

post.summary: Exchange an API key and secret for an SDK token
post.description:
The one endpoint your backend calls with the secret. The key prefix
decides the mode: `rk_live_` gives a live token, `rk_test_` a sandbox
one. Rate limited per address.

post.summary: Mint a short-lived token for one user's device
post.description:
Call this from your own backend, with a token from `/auth/token`. It
returns a token for one user, carrying only the scopes you ask for, and
it is what you hand your mobile app.

**Why this exists.** Every SDK's `initialize()` also accepts your API
key and secret, and anything compiled into a published app can be read
back out of it. A leaked live pair can create sessions billed to you
and list every session and call on your workspace. A device token can
do neither.

## Scopes

| Scope | Reaches |
|---|---|
| `sessions:verify` | `GET` and `POST /sessions/verify` |
| `sessions:read` | `GET /sessions/{id}`, and only sessions this user is a party to |
| `devices:write` | `POST` and `DELETE /devices/token`, `POST /devices/presence` |

Everything else refuses a device token with `403 scope-not-permitted`,
including creating, ending or retargeting a session, listing the
workspace's sessions or calls, and anything under `/config`,
`/billing`, `/webhooks`, `/numbers` or `/auth/keys`. A device token
also cannot mint another.

The WebSocket stream refuses device tokens: it fans out a whole
workspace's events, and narrowing it to one user is not built, so there
is no scope for it to grant.

## Lifetime

Fifteen minutes, and a floor of one minute. `ttlSeconds` outside that
is clamped rather than refused. Device tokens answer to the same
revocation as any other: suspending the workspace or rotating its API
key stops them on the next request.

userPhone.description: The user this token is for. A Nigerian mobile number.

ttlSeconds.description: Clamped into the window, never refused for being outside it.

403.description: A device token tried to mint another.

409.description: That email already has a workspace.

post.description: For a human in the console, not for an app. Rate limited to 10 attempts per 15 minutes per address.

200.description: A dashboard token, the user and the tenant.

post.description: Dashboard token, OWNER. Returns the new secret once; it is stored hashed and cannot be shown again.

post.summary: Issue API credentials for a mode
post.description: Dashboard token, OWNER. Live credentials are refused until business verification is approved; see `/auth/keys/requirements`.

200.description: The key and secret, secret shown once.

409.description: Requirements for live are not met.

post.description: Dashboard token, OWNER. Refused with the unmet items until every requirement passes.

409.description: Unmet requirements, listed in the body.

get.summary: What is still needed to go live

200.description: Each requirement and whether it is met.
The tenant, and the user if the token is a dashboard one.

patch.description:
Dashboard token, OWNER or ADMIN. Only the fields you send change.
`recordingEnabled: true` is refused with `422 feature-not-available`.

422.description: A field exists but the feature behind it does not.

post.description:
Allocates a proxy number for this pair and returns it. Both numbers must
be Nigerian mobile numbers in the same country.

The allocator guarantees no participant overlap: a number is never
serving two live sessions that share a party, which is what stops a
callback reaching the wrong person.

gracePeriodMinutes.description: Follow-up window after the session ends. Default 15.

recordingEnabled.description: Must be false or omitted. `true` is refused.

201.description: Session created and a proxy allocated.

422.description:
A number is not a Nigerian mobile, the two parties are in different
countries, or `recordingEnabled: true` was sent.

503.description: No number available, or the carrier breaker is open.

200.description: A page of sessions, newest first.

get.description:
Called by the SDK when the device is on a call. Answers whether that
call arrived through one of your live sessions in the last 60 seconds.

post.summary: Is this call really ours, as a POST
post.description: Same answer as the GET. Exists so the number can go in a body rather than a query string, which keeps it out of access logs and Referer headers.

patch.summary: Update metadata or the grace period

post.description:
Moves it to `GRACE_PERIOD`, so a follow-up call still connects. Send
`gracePeriodMinutes: 0` to cut contact off immediately.

patch.summary: Point the session at a different customer
patch.description:
Keeps the proxy number and swaps party B, for a reassigned order. The
previous customer stops reaching anyone on that number.

200.description: The session with the new target.

422.description: Not a Nigerian mobile, or it would collide on the proxy.

post.description:
Dashboard token, OWNER. Provisioning is a manual process today, so this
answers `501` and records the request. Ask us and we will size a pool.

200.description: The destination, the events, and recent deliveries.

post.description:
The URL must be public: a private, loopback or link-local address is
refused, and so is a redirect that lands on one. Deliveries are signed
with `X-Relavoi-Signature`, an HMAC of `timestamp.body`.

200.description: Registered. The secret is returned once if newly created.

422.description: The destination failed the SSRF guard.

post.description: Delivers a synthetic `session.created` to your registered URL, signed the same way a real one is, and reports what came back.

get.description:
Every attempt, with the status code your endpoint returned. The response
body and the error text are not included: they are operator-only.

200.description: A page of attempts, newest first.

post.description:
Stores an APNs or FCM token against a user and this tenant. Registration
works; nothing sends a notification to it yet.

delete.description: Call this on sign-out, or when the OS reports the token is stale.

200.description: Aggregates over calls in the window.
The counters your invoice is built from.
A page of periods, newest first.

get.description:
Billing is prepaid. `plan` is null only if your tier has no plan row,
which should not happen; if you see it, tell us rather than guessing a
price.

200.description: The wallet overview the dashboard renders.
A page of ledger entries, newest first.

post.description:
Opens a payment with the provider and returns where to send the payer.
Whole naira only. Confirm with the verify endpoint, or wait for the
provider callback, whichever arrives first; both are idempotent.

200.description: Where to send the payer, and the reference to verify.

503.description: Payments are not configured for this mode.

get.description: The provider fee is passed on, so the payer sees it before paying. VAT-exclusive.

post.description: Idempotent. Safe to call from the payer's return URL.

200.description: The outcome and the new balance.
Self-contained HTML, for printing or saving as PDF.
Status, what has been supplied, and what is missing.

post.description:
`multipart/form-data`, one file per request, with `kind` naming which
document it is. Stored encrypted; the operator console reads it through
a short-lived signed URL.

409.description: Already submitted, so it cannot be removed.

post.description: Refused with the missing items if anything required is absent.
